answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with staked identity. Each participant locks collateral and registers one public key; verifiers accept a vote only if its signature traces to a distinct funded stake. Spawning a thousand fake agents therefore needs a thousand separate deposits, so the attacker pays a roughly linear capital cost per fake identity, and any detected double-vote slashes that deposit. Hiding a bot on a frozen tundra or a lonely knoll still costs the same bond, and each accepted action leaves one auditable thread from the signature back to the locked collateral.
